column1: baseline-contrast|I|I1|wstg|A changed request produces a different page once. What best distinguishes a repeatable input effect from normal variation?|Repeat matched baseline and modified requests|Report the first difference as confirmed exploitation|Compare two unrelated endpoints only|Infer impact from the parameter's name|Controlled comparisons reveal whether input consistently causes the observation. Dynamic content and caching can create unrelated differences.|A response difference is a lead, not its explanation.

entry-headers|I|I1|wstg|A tester inventories only form fields. Which possible injection inputs are omitted?|Headers, cookies, paths, and API bodies|Only the site's static logo colors|Only the server's physical power cable|Only the certificate authority's office address|Applications may use many request fields as data. Identify how inputs reach processing paths rather than relying on visible forms.|Input location does not determine trust.

hidden-field|I|I1|authz|An accountId field is hidden in HTML. How should an authorized tester treat it?|As modifiable client input|As server-only trusted state|As an encrypted authorization decision|As a browser-enforced immutable value|Hidden fields are submitted by the client and can be altered. Verify server-side authorization on the selected account.|Visibility is not integrity.

disabled-field|I|I1|authz|The UI disables the role selector for ordinary users. What test checks actual enforcement?|Submit the role change directly as an ordinary user|Inspect only the selector's grey color|Ask an administrator to submit the same request|Count the options in the DOM|The endpoint should reject unauthorized role changes irrespective of frontend controls.|Test with the principal whose restriction matters.

hpp-first-last|I|I1|hpp|A proxy checks the first role parameter; the backend uses the last. Why is role=user&role=admin significant?|The components make different security decisions|All duplicate parameters are invalid in every protocol|The values are automatically encrypted together|The request must execute JavaScript|Different handling of duplicate values can bypass validation. Establish actual interpretation by each relevant component.|Parser disagreement matters more than duplication alone.

query-body|I|I1|hpp|Authorization reads accountId from the query, while execution reads it from the POST body. What should be tested?|Conflicting values across both locations|Only whether POST has a Content-Length|Only the spelling of the form title|Only whether the query ends with a slash|A mismatch may authorize one object and operate on another. Align authorization and execution on the same validated value.|The check must cover the object actually used.

encoded-location|I|I1|wstg|A percent-encoded marker appears literally on one page but decoded on another. What is the useful inference?|The processing paths handle encoding differently|Both paths necessarily have exploitable XSS|The TLS certificates differ in key length|Every parameter is stored in SQL|Map decoding and rendering before choosing context-specific tests. Encoding differences alone do not prove a vulnerability.|Follow the representation through the processing chain.

method-coverage|I|I1|authz|GET /document/9 enforces ownership. PUT on the same path has not been tested. What remains uncertain?|Authorization for the update operation|Whether the GET response has an HTML title|Whether the document ID is decimal|Whether the browser caches a favicon|Permissions and routing can differ by method. Test the relevant read, update, and delete paths separately.|A protected read path does not prove a protected write path.

content-type-path|I|I1|rest|JSON requests are validated, but equivalent form requests enter another handler. What should an assessment cover?|Both accepted parsing paths|Only JSON because it is modern|Only requests with the shortest body|Only the handler with the longest function name|Alternative encodings can invoke distinct validation or binding behavior.|Coverage follows accepted behavior, not the preferred client format.

negative-control-web|I|I1|wstg|A callback is observed after a test request. Which check strengthens attribution?|A distinct marker plus a matched negative control|Reuse one marker across every concurrent test|Assume every DNS callback came from execution|Delete the baseline response|Unique correlation and controls help identify what caused an interaction. Logging, scanners, or other components can also make requests.|Attribute the observation to the tested behavior.

session-replay|I|I1|session|To verify logout invalidation, which comparison is most direct?|Replay the same session credential after logout|Check that the logout button disappears|Compare two newly registered usernames|Search only for a cookie banner|The server should reject the former credential. Browser UI changes do not demonstrate revocation.|Observe authorization at the server after the state change.

cross-account|I|I1|authz|For an object authorization test, why use two controlled accounts with separate objects?|To distinguish ownership boundaries from missing objects|To double the number of passwords in the report|To ensure both accounts have administrator roles|To make the response bodies identical|Known owned objects allow meaningful permitted and denied comparisons without relying on guessed nonexistent IDs.|Choose evidence that isolates the authorization decision.

cache-control-test|I|I1|http|A modified response is identical to baseline and includes a cache-hit marker. What should be checked before concluding the input is ignored?|Whether caching prevented backend processing|Whether every HTTP method is forbidden|Whether the parameter is a public key|Whether the server uses a graphical desktop|Caches can mask differences. Understand cache keys and safely obtain appropriate origin observations within scope.|The response may not reflect execution of this request.

redirect-result|I|I1|http|A request returns 302. What is necessary before interpreting the final page as evidence?|Inspect the redirect and relevant final response|Treat every redirect as an authentication bypass|Ignore the Location header|Assume the original request returned the final body|Redirection can change location, method handling, and authentication context. Preserve the chain needed to explain behavior.|A final page does not describe every intermediate response.

minimal-proof|I|I1|wstg|A harmless unique marker demonstrates an authorized injection path. What is the best next reporting choice?|Document the bounded proof and supported consequence|Extract all customer records to maximize certainty|Claim operating-system takeover without evidence|Replace the marker with a destructive query|Evidence should support the stated result with minimal unnecessary effects. Distinguish demonstrated behavior from potential consequences.|A stronger claim needs stronger evidence, not more damage.

quote-error|I|I3|sqli|Adding a quote causes a 500 response. What is established at this point?|An input-dependent error needing investigation|Confirmed extraction of all database records|Confirmed database administrator access|Confirmed absence of validation everywhere|An error may come from SQL or other parsers. Repeat and identify the failure before claiming SQL injection.|A common probe is not proof of its intended mechanism.

paired-boolean|I|I3|wstg|Which result best supports Boolean-based SQL injection rather than random page variation?|Repeated opposite outcomes for matched true/false predicates|One slower request after network congestion|One page containing the word database|A certificate issued by a familiar authority|Matched predicates isolate a logical effect, especially with stable baselines and controls. Still document the affected input and behavior.|Change one meaningful condition at a time.

time-control|I|I3|wstg|A time-based SQL probe is slow once. What should happen before confirmation?|Repeat conditional probes and comparable controls|Assume the delay equals database execution|Disable all server timeouts|Report the exact number of database rows|Network load and other processing can cause latency. Conditional, repeatable differences strengthen the SQL hypothesis.|Timing evidence needs noise controls.

blind-definition|I|I3|wstg|SQL injection changes page behavior but displays no query data or detailed errors. Which description fits?|Blind inference may still be possible|SQL injection is ruled out|The database must be SQLite|Only stored XSS can explain this|SQL injection need not display results directly. Logical or timing effects can expose information indirectly.|Absence of a data dump is not absence of injection.

union-count|I|I3|wstg|A UNION query fails because its result has two columns while the original query has three. What requirement was violated?|Matching column count|Matching table name length|Matching HTTP status number|Matching database username length|UNION operands must have compatible result shapes, including equal column counts and compatible types.|A payload can be syntactically plausible yet incompatible with the query.

union-type|I|I3|wstg|UNION operands have equal column counts but incompatible data types. What follows?|The operation can still fail|It must always return the desired text|It changes all columns to passwords|It proves parameterized execution|Matching counts is not sufficient; type compatibility and DBMS conversion rules also matter.|Result shape includes types as well as count.

numeric-context|I|I3|sqli|Input is concatenated into WHERE id=<input>, without quotes. Why is testing only a quote incomplete?|The sink is a numeric expression context|Numbers cannot appear in SQL syntax|Numeric columns always use stored procedures|HTTP automatically escapes numeric inputs|Choose tests for the actual syntax context and prefer bound numeric values in remediation.|A string-literal payload is not universal.

like-boundary|I|I3|sqli|A bound LIKE value contains %. Does wildcard matching alone prove SQL injection?|No; wildcard semantics differ from query-structure injection|Yes; every wildcard executes another statement|Yes; bound parameters cannot contain symbols|No; because SQL has no LIKE operator|Binding prevents the value becoming SQL structure, but search semantics may still require wildcard handling.|Injection safety and intended matching behavior are separate.

order-allowlist|I|I3|sqli|A query binds its search term but concatenates the sort direction. What remains to inspect?|The unbound query-structure fragment|Only the bound term's Unicode font|Only whether the table has an index|Only whether results are paginated|Safe handling of one value does not secure other constructed syntax. Map sort choices to fixed permitted fragments.|Review the full query construction.

stored-procedure|I|I3|sqli|A stored procedure builds dynamic SQL by concatenating its input. Is the procedure name itself a defense?|No; the dynamic SQL still needs safe construction|Yes; all procedures automatically parameterize strings|Yes; procedures cannot accept attacker input|No; stored procedures never run on a database|Stored procedures are safe when implemented safely; dynamic concatenation can reintroduce injection.|A wrapper does not remove an unsafe sink.

second-order|I|I3|sqli|A name is safely stored with a bound INSERT, then concatenated into an administrative SQL query later. What risk exists?|Second-order SQL injection|Only reflected XSS|Only a TCP retransmission|Only DNS cache poisoning|Stored data can remain attacker-controlled. Safe insertion does not make later SQL construction safe.|Trust is not gained merely by passing through storage.

orm-raw|I|I3|sqli|An ORM is used, but a raw-query function interpolates user input. Which conclusion is correct?|The raw query still needs parameterization|The ORM guarantees all raw strings are safe|SQL injection is possible only without any ORM|Escaping HTML makes the query safe|Review raw-query and expression APIs separately from safe model operations.|Framework presence is not evidence of safe use.

least-privilege-sql|I|I3|sqli|Two apps have the same injection flaw, but one database account can only read one view. What does the restriction change?|The accessible capabilities and potential impact|Whether concatenation becomes parameterization|Whether the SQL parser recognizes quotes|Whether HTML is valid|Least privilege limits consequences without fixing injection. Document both the flaw and the account's effective rights.|Mitigation of impact is distinct from removal of the cause.

stacked-driver|I|I3|wstg|An injected second SQL statement is rejected. What must not be inferred?|That all SQL injection is impossible|That this multi-statement attempt failed|That driver behavior matters|That other query contexts need examination|Drivers and settings may reject stacked statements while other injection techniques remain feasible.|One failed technique does not close the vulnerability class.

db-errors-dialect|I|I3|wstg|A database error suggests SQL Server. How should this be used?|As a fingerprinting clue to verify|As proof of sysadmin rights|As proof of the exact patch level|As proof that every SQL Server feature is enabled|Error text can guide DBMS-specific reasoning, but version and privileges require separate evidence.|Product identification does not establish capabilities.

read-vs-write|I|I3|wstg|A controlled SQL test confirms unintended SELECT results. What does it directly demonstrate?|A read effect in the tested query context|The ability to delete every table|Operating-system command execution|The ability to reset every user password|Other effects may be possible but are not established by this observation. State proven and inferred consequences separately.|Do not silently escalate the evidence.

param-inside-quotes|I|I3|sqli|A developer puts the text '?' inside SQL quotes rather than using the driver's placeholder API. What may happen?|It becomes a literal character instead of a bound parameter|It always binds every submitted field|It turns the query into HTML|It encrypts the question mark|Placeholders must be used according to the driver's syntax and binding mechanism. Quoted text can be a literal.|Parameterization is an API operation, not a visual symbol.

validation-only|I|I3|sqli|An allowlist accepts numeric IDs but another string search input is concatenated. Which remediation is needed there?|Bind the string value through the database API|Remove only spaces from the search text|Require one digit somewhere in the string|Hide the search form from navigation|Validation can support business constraints; parameter binding protects the SQL data boundary.|One safely constrained input does not cover another sink.

wide-encoding|I|I3|sqli|Why can manual SQL escaping fail when client and server character handling disagree?|Bytes may be interpreted differently at the SQL parser|Character encodings always remove all apostrophes|TLS forces every query to ASCII|All databases share one escaping grammar|Prefer parameterization and consistent supported client encodings. Escaping correctness depends on the actual DBMS and encoding context.|A copied escaping recipe may not fit the connection.

transaction-test|I|I3|wstg|A test plan proposes writes inside a transaction that is rolled back. What still needs consideration?|Triggers, external effects, and actual rollback coverage|Only the page's background color|The assumption that transactions undo all network effects|The assumption that every statement starts its own safe sandbox|Not every consequence is transactional; scope, side effects, and cleanup must be understood before write testing.|Rollback is useful but not a universal undo mechanism.

test-precision|I|I3|wstg|A payload changes both a filter and a sort expression. Why is a narrower probe preferable?|It makes the causal effect easier to attribute|It guarantees higher database privilege|It prevents the server from logging the request|It reveals all schema names automatically|A minimal controlled variation reduces ambiguity about which input or syntax caused the result.|More syntax can mean less clear evidence.

reflection-marker|I|I2|xss|A marker is reflected as escaped text in HTML. What is demonstrated?|Reflection, without execution evidence|Confirmed JavaScript execution|Confirmed theft of an HttpOnly cookie|Confirmed database injection|Inspect the output context and escaping before assessing whether executable syntax can be introduced.|Reflection and XSS are different observations.

attribute-context|I|I2|xss|Input lands inside a quoted HTML attribute. What must a test consider?|The quote delimiter and attribute semantics|Only whether the HTML has a title tag|Only whether the value contains a digit|Only the browser window width|Attribute contexts differ from plain text and from URL or event-handler contexts. Determine the consuming grammar.|The same bytes can have different meanings in different sinks.

textarea-context|I|I2|xss|A marker is inside a textarea element. Why examine its exact rendering context?|Breaking out of the text element differs from plain HTML insertion|Textareas execute every submitted value automatically|Textareas always remove every closing tag before parsing|A textarea proves server-side code execution|Determine whether delimiters are encoded and whether the value remains inert text. Do not assume all HTML locations behave alike.|Element context changes the relevant boundary.

js-string-context|I|I2|xss|A search term is inserted into a JavaScript string in an inline script. Which boundary is relevant?|JavaScript string syntax and script-element parsing|Only SQL numeric literal syntax|Only SMTP envelope syntax|Only NTFS inheritance flags|Nested contexts require appropriate handling for both layers or a safer design that avoids inline executable insertion.|The outer HTML and inner language can both matter.

json-content-type|I|I2|xss|An API returns user text in application/json. Does finding angle brackets there prove XSS?|No; execution depends on subsequent handling|Yes; JSON always executes HTML tags|Yes; angle brackets grant browser administrator rights|No; JSON can never be consumed unsafely|Raw JSON text is not automatically HTML execution. Trace whether a client later inserts values into unsafe sinks.|Assess the whole data flow.

source-sink|I|I2|xss|Client code reads location.search and assigns it to innerHTML. Which evidence most directly supports DOM XSS?|A controlled source value reaching executable markup in that sink|Only a screenshot of the URL bar|Only the server returning status 200|Only the use of a JavaScript framework|Trace the attacker-controlled source, transformations, and dangerous sink, then verify browser behavior.|A source and a sink must be connected, not merely present.

hash-server|I|I2|xss|An XSS probe exists only after # in a URL. Why might server logs omit it?|The fragment is normally handled by the browser|HTTPS removes all path and query logging|Every fragment is sent as an SMTP header|The database strips all URL characters|Fragments generally are not part of the HTTP request. Client code can still use them unsafely.|No server log entry does not mean no client input.

stored-viewers|I|I2|xss|A submitted comment is safe on the public page but executes in a moderation view. What explains this?|Different rendering sinks for the same stored value|The comment became trusted through storage|All administrator browsers ignore HTML encoding|The TLS version changed the comment text|Each rendering path needs appropriate output handling. Test relevant audiences and contexts.|Safe output in one view does not secure all views.

safe-sink-retest|I|I2|xss|After replacing innerHTML with textContent, what retest demonstrates the intended fix?|The same input renders as text without creating injected elements|Only that the page still has a favicon|Only that the source file grew longer|Only that a scanner score increased|Verify the affected flow and expected functionality, not just a code change or score.|A remediation should be tested at the actual sink.

event-attribute|I|I2|xss|A sanitizer removes script elements but permits event-handler attributes. What gap remains?|Other executable markup can survive|All attributes are harmless without script elements|The browser automatically signs the remaining markup|Only the document's whitespace can change|XSS can use event handlers and other constructs. Use a robust permitted-markup policy rather than one-tag removal.|One payload family is not the entire attack surface.

sanitizer-mutate|I|I2|xss|A sanitized HTML string is subsequently concatenated with untrusted HTML before insertion. What must be reviewed?|The final combined content and processing order|Only the sanitizer's package logo|Only whether the first input was lowercase|Only the server's time zone|Later transformations can invalidate assumptions about sanitized data. Keep unsafe content out of the final sink.|A safe intermediate does not guarantee a safe final value.

csp-browser-proof|I|I2|csp|A payload appears in markup but CSP blocks execution in the tested browser. How should evidence be described?|Injection observed; execution blocked in the tested conditions|Confirmed unrestricted script execution|Confirmed absence of all markup injection|Confirmed database administrator access|Record both the root behavior and mitigation, without overstating or ignoring either. Examine realistic policy and browser conditions.|Blocked execution and safe output are distinct states.

encoded-not-decoded|I|I2|xss|A payload is stored as literal < text and remains literal through rendering. What should not be claimed from this alone?|Successful browser code execution|That input can be stored|That encoding affected the value|That the page renders text|Execution requires an interpretable path, not just recognizable payload text.|Visible attack syntax is not an executed attack.

url-sink-test|I|I2|xss|A link builder correctly quotes href but accepts script-capable schemes. Which test dimension matters?|URL scheme validation|Only quote escaping|Only CSS word wrapping|Only server socket backlog|Evaluate the value's semantics in addition to markup syntax. Safe URL schemes are context-dependent.|Syntactic escaping cannot make every URL safe.

browser-context|I|I2|wstg|A browser extension causes a popup during a test. Why is a clean controlled browser context useful?|It reduces unrelated sources of execution|It guarantees every web application is safe|It disables the need for response capture|It grants testing authorization automatically|Control the environment and preserve evidence connecting input to behavior. Extension activity can confound a test.|An observed popup needs an attributed cause.

authorization-token|I|I4|authz|A signed token carries role=user, but the server trusts an unsigned role field beside it. What test is relevant?|Alter the unsigned field while keeping the signed token intact|Break the token signature in every test only|Inspect only the token's Base64 alphabet|Check only the certificate expiration date|Trusted identity evidence does not automatically authenticate adjacent client fields.|A valid signature covers specified bytes, not the whole request.

base64-trust|I|I4|authz|An authorization state is merely Base64-encoded in a cookie. What does Base64 provide?|Reversible representation|Authenticity against tampering|Confidentiality against a reader|Authorization for arbitrary roles|Encoding is not signing or encryption. Assess whether the server verifies integrity and permitted state.|Recognizing an encoded format is only the first step.

role-method-test|I|I4|authz|A user receives 403 on an admin GET but succeeds with an equivalent POST. What has been shown?|Method-dependent authorization inconsistency|A broken public certificate|A mandatory browser cache update|A SQL Server database restore|Enforcement can differ across handlers. Verify intended operation and resulting state, not just status codes.|Permission rules must cover every accepted route to an operation.

status-only|I|I4|authz|An unauthorized update returns 403, but the record changes anyway. What is the key observation?|The forbidden side effect occurred|The status code proves complete protection|The client necessarily changed only its cache|A 403 cannot accompany a state change|Check state through an appropriate controlled observation. A response label cannot undo an operation.|Enforcement is about effects as well as messages.

multi-step-bypass|I|I4|authz|A checkout validates discount eligibility on step one, but step three accepts a modified discount ID without rechecking. What should be tested?|Authorization and integrity at the final operation|Only whether step one renders a green badge|Only whether the discount ID has eight digits|Only whether the user has a recent cookie|Intermediate UI checks do not secure later independently callable steps. Bind or recompute trusted transaction state.|Every consequential operation needs its own trusted inputs.

race-balance|I|I4|authz|Two concurrent withdrawals both pass a balance check and overdraw the account. What is the relevant failure?|Non-atomic validation and update|Incorrect HTML entity encoding|An expired DNS TTL|A missing password complexity message|Protect consistency with appropriate atomic operations, locking, or transaction isolation. A rule can be correct yet raced.|Sequential tests may miss concurrency behavior.

reset-old-password|I|I4|reset|After a reset, a second login using the old password still succeeds. Which test distinguishes real persistence from a cached page?|Perform a fresh authentication with the old credential|Reload only the password-reset success page|Count the characters in the reset token|Change only the browser language|Verify authentication against the server rather than a previously authenticated session or cached view.|A live session does not prove an old password remains valid.

token-expiry|I|I4|session|A token says it expires at noon, but the server accepts it at 13:00. What must enforcement check?|The server's validated expiry decision and clock handling|Only the decoded token's visual layout|Only whether a client displays an expiry warning|Only whether the token has three segments|Claims need validated, server-enforced semantics and appropriate clock assumptions.|Readable expiry metadata is not enforced expiry.

non-admin-read|I|I4|authz|A normal user can download the admin report but cannot run the admin dashboard. How should this be classified?|Unauthorized access to the report|Full administrator takeover by definition|Only a harmless UI inconsistency|Only missing password salting|The accessed resource determines the supported claim. Different administrative functions can have separate controls.|Describe the precise resource and authority gained.

field-sensitive|I|I4|authz|A user can read their own profile but a query flag reveals internal fraud notes too. Which boundary is at issue?|Field-level authorization|Only transport encryption|Only username uniqueness|Only HTML text length|Access to an object does not automatically authorize every property or related dataset.|Test the returned fields as well as the object ID.

alternate-channel|I|I4|authz|The web UI correctly restricts a record, but a mobile API exposes it to the same user. What should remediation cover?|All relevant access paths to the resource|Only the desktop navigation bar|Only browser-specific CSS|Only the mobile app's icon|Apply consistent server-side permissions across channels and services.|The resource's policy must survive alternate clients.

error-vs-access|I|I4|wstg|Changing an object ID yields an error containing another user's name but no full record. What is supported?|Information disclosure in the tested error path|Confirmed modification of the other account|Confirmed execution of arbitrary commands|Confirmed absence of any privacy impact|Limited disclosure can be meaningful; document exact data and reproducibility without claiming unobserved access.|Impact can be narrower than full object retrieval.

state-recheck|I|I4|authz|A user is authorized when a job is queued, but loses access before a sensitive export executes. What policy question matters?|Whether execution must recheck current authority|Whether the queue name contains digits|Whether the browser can keep a tab open|Whether every queued job uses HTTP GET|Long-running workflows need a deliberate policy for identity, authorization lifetime, and revocation.|A permission decision has a time context.

evidence-redaction|I|I4|wstg|A controlled account proves cross-user access. Which report evidence is most useful?|Exact reproduction and minimally necessary proof of the crossed boundary|A claim that every user is compromised without testing|A screenshot only of the website homepage|An unrelated vulnerability scanner score|Explain principal, request, target object, observed data or state, and controls. Avoid unnecessary collection beyond the proof.|Make the authority failure reproducible and specific.

dom-safe-api|I|I2|xss|A review finds a user value passed to createTextNode. What is the immediate sink behavior?|Creating a text node rather than parsing HTML|Executing the value as JavaScript|Treating the value as a SQL expression|Granting the value same-origin credentials|A text-node API is appropriate for text output. Trace other uses of the value independently.|A safe sink should be recognized as well as an unsafe one.

authz-cached-claim|I|I4|authz|A removed role still works only on one API instance. What comparison helps isolate the cause?|The same principal and operation across instances|Different users making unrelated requests|Only the load balancer's logo|Only the site's public robots.txt|Instance-specific caches or deployment differences may explain inconsistent authorization. Keep identity, operation, and state controlled.|Distribution can make a security rule inconsistent.

blind-oob-limit|I|I3|wstg|A SQL-related external callback is observed, but no rows were returned. What should the evidence claim?|The attributed interaction and its demonstrated mechanism|A complete database dump|The password of every database account|Guaranteed operating-system administrator access|Out-of-band observations can confirm a path without proving data extraction or maximum privilege.|Describe the bytes and behavior actually observed.

quote-count|I|I3|sqli|An input containing an apostrophe works correctly after a parameterization fix. What further check is useful?|That hostile syntax remains data while legitimate input still works|Only that all apostrophes are permanently banned|Only that the application changed its logo|Only that the query is now longer|Verify the relevant attack boundary alongside ordinary names and search values containing punctuation.|A fix should preserve supported data, not just reject a probe.

stored-output-multi|I|I2|xss|An encoded stored value is safe in HTML text but inserted raw into a later script. What does the first safe view prove?|Only that the tested rendering path handled it safely|That the stored value is safe in every context|That all later JavaScript is parameterized|That no user can modify the original field|Review each source-to-sink path and its context. Encoding suited to one output is not a permanent trust label.|Safety belongs to a use, not merely a value.
